stem: When teaching home infection-prevention measures after transplantation, which medication-related step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Complete medication for infection prophylaxis or treatment as directed
Stop all infection prophylaxis once the recipient feels well
Infection prophylaxis is optional and never needs to be completed
Prophylaxis should be shared with household members instead of the recipient

explanation.rationale_correct: Infection-prevention teaching includes completing medication for infection prophylaxis or treatment as directed, along with wound care and other household precautions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Prophylaxis and treatment courses should be completed as directed rather than stopped when the recipient feels well.
rationale_incorrect.C: Completing prescribed prophylaxis or treatment is specifically recommended.
rationale_incorrect.D: The recipient completes their own prescribed prophylaxis rather than transferring it to household members.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → vi. Others
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Complete medication for infection prophylaxis or treatment as directed

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → vi. Others (complete infection prophylaxis/treatment as directed); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Prophylaxis-completion teaching angle distinct from wound-cleaning precaution (cctc-1143) and CMV prophylaxis discharge teaching (cctc-3026); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A transplant recipient asks what donor-related information may be shared when it affects informed consent. Which example aligns with standard donor–recipient confidentiality references?

options.text: Organ characteristics or an anatomic abnormality that could affect organ function
The donor family's unrelated vacation itinerary
Unrelated donor employment history with no clinical relevance

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipients may be informed of specific donor information critical to informed consent, including possible donor-transmitted disease risks and organ characteristics or anatomic abnormality that could affect organ function.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donor family vacation plans are not clinically relevant donor disclosure examples.
rationale_incorrect.C: Staff personal schedules are not part of donor information shared for consent.
rationale_incorrect.D: Unrelated employment history without clinical relevance is not required donor disclosure.

stem: When teaching about donor–recipient confidentiality after transplantation, which communication point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Donor families will receive a letter from the OPO within 30 days of the donation
Donor families never receive any communication from the OPO after donation
Recipient identifying information is always shared with donor families without restriction
OPO communication with donor families occurs only after ten years

explanation.rationale_correct: The OPO may provide general recipient status information to the donor family as part of organ allocation, and donor families will receive a letter from the OPO within 30 days of donation.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donor families receive OPO communication including a letter within 30 days rather than no contact.
rationale_incorrect.C: Only general information such as age decade, health status, and gender may be provided without recipient permission.
rationale_incorrect.D: Communication occurs within 30 days rather than being deferred for a decade.

stem: A coordinator is updating infection-prevention and donor-confidentiality teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should complete medication for infection prophylaxis or treatment as directed.
Recipients may be informed of organ characteristics or anatomic abnormality that could affect organ function.
Donor families never receive any communication from the OPO after donation.
Shedding after live-virus vaccination may continue for days, weeks, or months.

explanation.rationale_correct: Completing prophylaxis, clinically relevant donor anatomic disclosure, and prolonged live-vaccine shedding precautions are supported. Statement III is false because donor families receive an OPO letter within 30 days of donation.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—live-vaccine shedding may persist for a variable period.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because OPO communication with donor families occurs after donation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention and p. Donor–recipient confidentiality
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Complete medication for infection prophylaxis … Organ characteristics or anatomic abnormality … letter from the OPO within 30 days … Shedding after vaccination with live virus vaccines may continue for days, weeks or months

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → vi. and p. Donor–recipient confidentiality → i.–ii. (prophylaxis completion, anatomic disclosure, OPO letter, live-vaccine shedding); PDF p. 117 and p. 122 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
